title: Integrated Nutrient Diagnosis: Symptoms, Tissue and Root-Zone Evidence

content.overview: Visual symptoms are useful observations but are not unique diagnoses. Similar discoloration, necrosis or growth changes can result from nutrient supply, root damage, pH, salinity, irrigation, disease or environment. Diagnosis improves when multiple evidence streams agree.

vocabulary.definition: An observable plant response that may have multiple possible causes.
Laboratory measurement of elemental concentrations in sampled plant tissue.
A structured comparison of plausible causes followed by tests that discriminate among them.

sections.title: Pattern comes before label
sections.body: Record where symptoms start, which leaves are affected, how rapidly they progress and whether they align with irrigation zones, cultivars or environmental gradients before naming a deficiency.

sections.title: Tissue results need sampling context
sections.body: Cannabis deficiency research showed that visual onset did not always align simply with foliar elemental concentrations. Leaf age, canopy position, sampling time and reference ranges influence interpretation.

sections.title: Root-zone and environment can mimic nutrition problems
sections.body: EC, pH, water status, oxygenation and root disease can change uptake even when nutrients are present. A feed-sheet comparison alone cannot distinguish these mechanisms.

workedExamples: Interveinal chlorosis appearing only in one irrigation zone warrants checking root-zone pH/EC and delivery uniformity before increasing a micronutrient.
A tissue value outside a published range should be interpreted with the sampled leaf position and crop stage rather than treated as an automatic correction command.
commonMistakes: Changing several inputs before collecting baseline data.
content.practicalApplication: Create a diagnostic worksheet with symptom map, timeline, cultivar, stage, irrigation zone, root observations, input/runoff or solution data, environmental history and tissue results. Rank hypotheses and change one controllable factor at a time where practical.
content.summary: Reliable nutrient diagnosis triangulates symptoms, plant tissue, root-zone conditions and environmental context.
